chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi.

He said: While I was standing before Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), he said to me: O Abu al-Salt! Enter this dome in which is the grave of Harun [al-Rashid] and bring me earth from its four sides. He said: I went and brought it. When I presented myself before him, he said: Give me the earth that is near the door. I gave it to him; he took it, smelled it, then threw it. Then he said: A grave will be dug for me here, and a rock will appear; even if every pickaxe in Khurasan were gathered against it, it would not be possible to uproot it.

a rock [will appear — and] even if every pickaxe in Khurasan were gathered against it, it would not be possible to uproot it. Then he said: What is at the foot and what is at the head [of the grave site] is likewise. Then he said: Give me this dust, for it is from my burial ground. Then he said: A grave will be dug for me in this place, so order them to dig seven steps downward and to carve a tomb-niche for me. If they refuse and offer only a lateral grave, then order them to make the lateral niche two arm-lengths and a handspan, for God, Mighty and Majestic, will expand it for me as He wills. When they do that, you will see moisture near my head. Speak the words I will teach you, and the water will spring forth until the niche is filled. You will see small fish therein, so crumble [bread]

the bread I will give you, and they will pick it up. When none of it remains, a large fish will emerge from it and devour the small fish until none of them remain. Then it will disappear. When it disappears, place your hand upon

the water, and speak the words I will teach you, and it will recede until nothing remains. Do not do this except in the presence of al-Ma'mun. Then he (peace be upon him) said: O Abu al-Salt! Tomorrow I will enter upon this transgressor. If I come out with my head uncovered, then speak to me and I will speak to you. If I come out with my head covered, do not speak to me. Abu al-Salt said: When we woke the following morning, he put on his clothes and sat in his prayer niche waiting. While he was thus, the servant of al-Ma'mun entered and said to him: Answer the Commander of the Faithful. So he put on his sandals and his cloak, and walked while I followed him, until he entered upon al-Ma'mun, before whom was a plate of grapes and plates of fruit, and in his hand was a bunch of grapes of which he had eaten some and left some. When he saw al-Rida (blessings of God upon him), he leapt toward him, embraced him, and kissed between his eyes, and sat him beside him. Then he offered him

the bunch [of grapes] and said: O son of the Messenger of God! Have you seen grapes more beautiful than these? So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to him: Perhaps there are beautiful grapes that come from Paradise. So he said to him: Eat from it. So al-Rida (peace be upon him) said to him: Would you excuse me from it? He said: There is no escaping it. What prevents you from it? Perhaps you suspect us of something? So he took the bunch and ate from it. Then he passed it to him, and al-Rida (peace be upon him) ate three grapes from it. Then he set it aside and stood up. So [al-Ma'mun] said

to him: Where are you going? He said: To where you have directed me. So he (peace be upon him) left with his head covered. I did not speak to him until he entered the house. He ordered the gate to be locked, so it was locked. Then he lay down on his bed. I remained standing in the courtyard of the house, anxious and grieving; until a youth with a handsome face and curly hair entered — the person most resembling al-Rida (peace be upon him). I rushed to him and said

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) then said: Stand, O Abu al-Salt, and bring me a washing basin and water from the storeroom. So I said: There is no washing basin or water in the storeroom! So he said: Do what I command you to do. So I entered the storeroom, and behold, there was a washing basin and water. I brought them out and rolled up my sleeves to wash him alongside him. But he said to me: Step aside, O Abu al-Salt, for I have one other than you to assist me. So he washed him. Then he said to me: Enter the storeroom and bring me the basket that contains his shroud and embalming spices. So I entered, and there was a basket I had not seen in that storeroom before. I carried it to him, and he shrouded him and prayed over him. Then he said: Bring me the coffin. So I said: Should I go to the carpenter to have a coffin made? He said: Rise, for there is a coffin in the storeroom. So I entered the storeroom and there was a coffin I had never seen before. I brought it to him. Then he took al-Rida (peace be upon him), after having prayed over him, and placed him in the coffin and arranged his feet. He prayed two units of prayer and had not finished them when the coffin rose up and the ceiling split open, and the coffin passed through it and departed.

So I said: O son of the Messenger of God! At this moment al-Ma'mun will come to us and demand al-Rida (peace be upon him) from me. What should I do? He said: Be silent, for he will return. O Abu al-Salt, there is no prophet who dies in the East whose successor dies in the West except that God, Mighty and Majestic, gathers their spirits and their bodies together. He had not finished speaking when the ceiling split open and the coffin descended. He (peace be upon him) stood up, took al-Rida (peace be upon him) out of the coffin, and placed him on his bed as though he had not been washed or shrouded. And he said: O Abu al-Salt! Stand and open the gate for al-Ma'mun.

So I opened the gate, and al-Ma'mun and his servants were at the gate. He entered weeping and grieving, his collar torn, striking his head, saying: O my master! I am bereaved of you, my master. Then he entered, sat at his head, and said: Prepare him for burial. He proceeded to the digging of the grave. I attended the spot, and everything appeared as al-Rida (peace be upon him) had described. One of his companions said to him: Do you not claim that he was an Imam? He said: Yes. An Imam is none but the foremost in rank. So he ordered that a grave be dug facing the qibla. So I said: He ordered me to dig seven steps and to carve a tomb-niche for him. He said: Do what Abu al-Salt commands you, except for the tomb-niche — instead dig and make a lateral niche.

When he saw what appeared of the moisture, the fish, and other things, al-Ma'mun said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) never ceased showing us his marvels in his lifetime, until he showed them to us after his death. A vizier who was with him said: Do you know what al-Rida was informing you? He said: No. He said: Surely he was informing you that your kingdom — the Abbasids — with your multitudes and the length of your reign, is like these small fish; until when your appointed terms expire, your traces are cut off, and your state vanishes, God, Blessed and Exalted, will empower a man from us against you to destroy every last one of you. He said to him: You have spoken the truth.

Then he said to me: O Abu al-Salt! Teach me the words you spoke. I said: By God, I forgot the words in that very moment — and I had spoken the truth. So he ordered that I be imprisoned. Al-Rida (peace be upon him) was buried, and I was imprisoned for a year. The prison became oppressive to me, and I stayed awake at night. So I supplicated to God, Mighty and Majestic, with a supplication in which I mentioned Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), and I asked God by their right to relieve me. I had not finished the supplication when Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) entered upon me. He said to me: O Abu al-Salt! Has your chest constricted? So I said: Yes, by God. He said: Stand and depart. Then he struck my shackles with his hand, and they fell away. He took me by my hand and brought me out of the house. The guards and servants saw me but were unable to speak to me. I exited through the front gate. Then he said: Go in the trust of God, for you will not reach him, nor will he ever reach you. Abu al-Salt said: I have not met with al-Ma'mun from that day to this.

key_terms.الرضا: Al-Rida — Imam Ali ibn Musa, the eighth Imam, poisoned by the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun in 203 AH
key_terms.الضريحة: Tomb-niche (darih) — a coffin-shaped excavation within a grave, distinct from a lateral niche (lahd)
key_terms.المأمون: Al-Ma'mun — Abbasid caliph (r. 813–833 CE) who brought al-Rida to Khurasan and is believed to have poisoned him
key_terms.المغتسل: Washing basin (mughtasal) — the vessel used for the ritual washing (ghusl) of the deceased
key_terms.حجة الله: Proof of God (Hujjat Allah) — a title of the Imam as God's authoritative representative on earth

ai.seo_question: What happened at the death of Imam al-Rida according to Abu al-Salt al-Harawi?
ai.summary: Abu al-Salt al-Harawi narrates a detailed eyewitness account of the death of Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) in Khurasan and the miraculous arrival of his son, Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (AS), who came from Medina to perform the funeral rites. The narrative details the Imam's foreknowledge of his own burial, the miraculous provisions for his washing and shrouding that appeared from the unseen, and his body's temporary disappearance and return. The account reflects the Shia doctrine of the Imam's supernatural knowledge and the transmission of the imamate to al-Jawad (AS), set against the backdrop of Abbasid political control under al-Ma'mun.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to me from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Abi’l Salt al-Harawi.

He said: I was standing before Abi’l Hasan `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as) when he said to me: O Aba’l Salt! Enter this dome in which is the grave of Harun [al-Rashid] and bring me dust from its four sides. He said: So, I went and brought it to him. When I came before him, he said to me: Give me the dust that is at the gate. So, I brought it to him, and he took it, smelled it, then dropped it. Then, he said: A grave will be dug for me here, and a rock will appear. Were you to bring every pickaxe in Khurasan, you would not be able to uproot it.

Then, he said: [The dust] that is at the person is like that which is at the head. Then, he said: Bring me this dust, for it is from my dust. Then, he said: [A grave] will be dug up for me at this place. So, order them to dig seven steps deep and create space for a tomb. If they refuse and offer a regular grave, then order them to extend the regular grave by two armlengths and a handspan, for Allah will extend it for me however He pleases. If they do it, you will see a creek at [the place for] my head. So, speak the words that I will teach you, and the water will fill up the grave.
You will see small fish therein. So, feed them the bread that I will give to you. When none of it is left, a large whale will come and devour the small fish until none are left. Then, it will leave.

Once it leaves, put your hand in the water, and speak the words that I will teach you, and it will recede until nothing is left of it. Do not do this except in the presence of al-Ma’mun. Then, he (as) said: O Aba’l Salt! Tomorrow morning, I will visit this transgressor. If my head is uncovered when I leave, then speak to me and I will speak to you. If my head is covered, then do not speak to me. Abu’l Salt said: When we awoke the next morning, he got dressed and sat waiting in his prayer-niche. He remained there until the slave of al-Ma’mun entered and said to him: Answer the commander of the faithful. So, he put on his sandals and his cloak, and he walked while I followed him. He entered the place of al-Ma’mun, and before him was a plate with grapes on it and plates with fruits on them. In his hand were a bunch of grapes, and he had eaten some and left some. When he saw al-Rida (s), he embraced him and kissed his forehead.

He sat him with him and passed the bunch to him, saying: O son of the Messenger of Allah! Have you seen grapes more beautiful than these? So, al-Rida (as) said to him: Perhaps beautiful grapes came from Paradise. So, he said to him: Eat from it. So, al-Rida (as) said to him: Would you excuse me from [eating from] it? So, he said: There is no need for that. What prevents you from it? Do you accuse us of something? He took it back and ate from it. Then, al-Rida (as) ate three grapes from it. Then, he put it away and stood up.

So, al-Ma’mun said to him: Where are you going? He said: To where you had sent me. So, he (as) left with his head covered. I did not speak to him until he entered the house. He ordered that the gate be locked, so it was locked. Then, he slept on his bed. So, I remained standing in the courtyard, concerned and distressed; until a youth with a beautiful face and short hair entered. He was the person who resembled al-Rida (as) the most. I rushed to him and said to him: Where did you enter from, considering the gate is locked? So, he said to me: The One who brought me here from Medina in this time is the same One who brought me into the house when the gate was locked. So, I said to him: Who are you? So, he said to me: I am the Proof of Allah over you, Aba’l Salt. I am Muhammad b. `Ali. Then, he went in the direction of his father (as) and entered. He commanded me to enter with him. When al-Rida (as) saw him, he embraced him, held him tightly to his chest, and kissed his forehead. Then, he brought him to his bed; and Muhammad b. `Ali (as) kissed him and whispered something to him that I did not understand. On the lips of al-Rida (as), I saw butter that was whiter than snow, and I saw Aba Ja`far [Muhammad b. `Ali al-Jawad] lick it with his tongue.

Then, he brought his hand between his robe and his chest, took out something that resembled a bird, and had Abu Ja`far (as) swallow it. Then, al-Rida (as) passed away. Abu Ja`far (as) then said: Stand, Aba’l Salt, and bring me a water basin and water from the closet. So, I said: There is no water basin or water in the closet! So, he said: Do what I command you to do. So, I entered the closet and found a water basin and water. I brought it to him, and I tied my clothes to my waist so that I could bathe him with him. So, he said to me: Go, Aba’l Salt, for surely, I have someone else to assist me. So, he washed him, and then said to me: Enter the closet and bring me the basket that has his shroud and embalmment in it. So, I entered, and I saw a basket that I had not seen before in that closet. So, I carried it to him, and he shrouded him and prayed over him. Then, he said: Bring me the coffin. So, I said: Go to the carpenter so that he could prepare a coffin. He said: Stand, for there is a coffin in the closet. So, I entered the closet and I saw a coffin that I had not seen before. Then, I brought it to him. So, he took al-Rida (as) after praying over him, and he placed him in the coffin and lined up his feet. He prayed two units and did not stop until the coffin was lifted up.

The ceiling cracked open, and the coffin went away. So, I said: O son of the Messenger of Allah! At this hour, al-Ma’mun will come to us, and he will demand al-Rida (as) from me. So, what should I do? So, he said: Be quiet, for he will return, Aba’l Salt. There is not a prophet who dies in the East who has his deputy die in the West except that Allah gathers their spirits and bodies together. He did not finish speaking until the roof cracked open [again] and the coffin came down. So, he (as) stood, took the body of al-Rida (as) out of the coffin, and placed it on his bed. It was as though he was not bathed or shrouded. He said: O Aba’l Salt! Stand and open the gate for al-Ma’mun.

So, I opened the gate, and I found al-Ma’mun and slaves at the gate. So, he entered weeping, grieving, with his pocket ripped, striking his face, saying: O master! I have panicked over you, master. Then, he entered, sat at his head, and said: Take him and prepare him. He passed by the digging of the grave – and I had prepared the spot, and everything that al-Rida (as) described had appeared. One of his guards said to him (al-Ma’mun): Do you not allege that he was an Imam? He said: Yes. He would not be an Imam if he had not been the head and the superior [of all people]. So, he commanded that a grave be dug facing the qibla. So, I said: He ordered me to dig seven steps deep and create space for a tomb. So, he said: Do as Abu’l Salt commands you to do, except regarding the tomb – dig a regular grave there.

When he saw what appeared from the creek, the whale, and other than that, al-Ma’mun said: Al-Rida (as) has not ceased in showing us his marvels in his life, to the point where he showed them to us after his death. So, a vizier who was with him said to him: Do you recognize what al-Rida is informing you through this? He said: No. He said: Surely, he is informing you that your kingdom – the Children of al-`Abbas – with your multitudes and the length of your term is like these [small] fish; until your ending comes and your state vanishes, and Allah empowers a man from us to finish every last one of you. He said to him: You have spoken the truth.

Then, he said to me: O Aba’l Salt! Teach me the words that you spoke. I said: By Allah, I have forgotten the words in this moment – and I had spoken the truth. So, he ordered that I be imprisoned. Al-Rida (as) was buried, and I was imprisoned for a year. The prison was narrow for me, and [one day,] I stayed up during the night. So, I supplicated to Allah with a supplication in which I mentioned Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad (as). I asked Allah, by their right, to relieve me. I did not conclude the supplication until Muhammad b. `Ali (as) visited me. He said to me: O Aba’l Salt! Has your chest tightened? So, I said: Yes, by Allah. He said: Stand and exit. Then, he struck my shackles with his hand, and they loosened. He took me by my hands and took me out of the [prison] house. The guards and the slaves saw me, but they were unable to speak to me. I exited from the front door. Then, he said: Go, in the trust of Allah. You will not reach him, nor will he reach you, ever. Abu’l Salt said: I haven not met with al-Ma’mun [again] till this day.
